chunks: From him, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbār, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from al-ʿAlāʾ ibn al-Fuḍayl, who said:

I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who is rendered unconscious for a day until night, then regains consciousness. He said: If he regains consciousness before sunset, then he must make up this day of his. And if he was unconscious for several numbered days, then he is not required to make up except the last of his days, if he regains consciousness before sunset; otherwise, there is no make-up upon him.

So the proper way regarding these reports is that we carry them upon a mode of recommendation, because the proofs indicate that making up what he missed during the state of unconsciousness is not obligatory upon him. These reports are thus understood as encouraging the making up of what he missed. As for the salat (prayer) whose time remains when he regains consciousness, then making it up is binding upon him in every case; that is indicated by the evidence.

key_terms.غُرُوبِ الشَّمْسِ: sunset, the cutoff point mentioned for the ruling
key_terms.قَضَاءُ: making up a missed religious duty

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on making up fasts or prayers missed due to unconsciousness in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the ruling on a person who misses fasting or salat (prayer) due to unconsciousness. It indicates that missed acts during unconsciousness are generally not obligatory to make up, though some reports encourage making them up as a recommended act, while any salat (prayer) whose time remains upon recovery must still be performed.
